lessons.title: Sealed Snack Bag Climb
beats: See Bag Swell Up: On the drive from Lukla base at 2860m to 4910m camp, a sealed chips bag swells tight and hard.: It is like a squeezed sponge slowly opening as hands lift off it.
Predict Using Oxygen Idea: You predict the bag swells because there is less oxygen higher up pushing back outside.
Spot Pressure Mismatch Clue: Total outside push drops even where oxygen share stays near 21 percent, so oxygen alone cannot explain it.

lessons.title: Weight of Air Above
beats: Feel Air Column Weight: Gravity pulls the whole air column down, and that weight squeezes air at the bottom.: It is like feeling heavier at the bottom of a pile of blankets.
Climb Above Air Mass: Climbing to 5000m leaves much air below you, so less air remains above pressing down.
Link Pressure To Altitude: Fewer air molecules above means lower weight, lower pressure, and thinner pressing on everything.

lessons.title: Guide Altimeter Calibration Job
beats: Record Base Camp Pressure: At surveyed 2860m benchmark, guide logs 72 kilopascals as signed base reading before clients ascend.
Check Higher Camp Reading: At 4910m high camp the altimeter shows near 55 kilopascals because less air presses above.
Sign Calibration Log Done: Guide writes weight-of-air reason in log, signs it, and clears altimeter for paid trek use.

evidence: There is less oxygen higher up.
fingerprint.reasoning: States pressure falls because there is less oxygen higher up.
fingerprint.misconception: altitude pressure falls due to less oxygen
fingerprint.intervention: Ask what presses down to make pressure and how much air is above at height.

questions.final_answer: There is less oxygen higher up.

steps.wrote: The ship floats because it is very light
and the nail sinks because it is heavier.
Heavy objects sink and light objects float.

questions.diagnosis: Explained floating by lightness alone instead of displaced water upthrust balancing weight.

check.why: The level replays the ship-versus-nail prediction in a harbour tank, teaches displacement and upthrust balance, and ends with loading a cargo barge to its safe displacement limit, with all claims physically correct.

holds.answered: Displacement does not matter; the light ship floats and the heavier nail sinks
The ship is very light and the nail is heavier, so heavy sinks and light floats
Judge by total heaviness alone, ignoring how much extra water the hull can displace

knows.answered: The wide hull displaces tonnes of water; the tiny nail displaces only a few drops
The ship's displaced water gives upthrust equal to its weight; the nail cannot displace enough water to balance its weight
Add crates only while each added tonne displaces one more tonne of water up to the hull limit

lessons.title: Predicting Ship and Nail
beats: Spot the weight trap: Many predict the steel ship floats because it is very light and the nail sinks because it is heavier.
Picture harbour test tank: A harbour tank shows a huge hollow steel ship beside a tiny solid nail ready for a float test.
Predict displaced water amounts: The wide hull can push aside tonnes of water while the nail pushes aside only a few drops.

lessons.title: Displaced Water Pushes Up
beats: Weigh pushed-aside water: Displaced water has weight, and that weight decides how hard the water pushes up.
Balance upthrust against weight: A floating object stays up when upthrust from displaced water equals its total downward weight.
Explain ship floats nail sinks: The hollow ship displaces enough water for large upthrust, but the solid nail cannot displace enough.

lessons.title: Load the Cargo Barge
beats: Read barge load chart: A cargo barge floats high empty and sits lower as crates add weight needing more upthrust.
Measure extra displacement needed: Each added tonne must push aside one more tonne of harbour water to keep upthrust balanced.
Decide safe crate limit: Check hull displacement limit from Question 24 to decide how many crates still float safely.

evidence: The ship floats because it is very light
and the nail sinks because it is heavier.
Heavy objects sink and light objects float.
fingerprint.reasoning: States heavy objects sink and light objects float regardless of displacement.
fingerprint.misconception: heavy sinks and light floats regardless of displacement
fingerprint.intervention: Compare heavy ship with tiny nail: predict displaced water and upthrust for each shape.

questions.final_answer: The ship floats because it is very light and the nail sinks because it is heavier. Heavy objects sink and light objects float.
